title: Our 2027 Innovators Under 35 competition is now open
gist: Promotional announcement that MIT Technology Review's 2027 Innovators Under 35 list is open for free nominations (including self-nominations) until 11:59 p.m. ET on Tuesday, January 19. Little investment signal beyond the list serving as a scouting pipeline for young researchers and founders.

insights.claim: MIT Technology Review's 2027 Innovators Under 35 competition is open for free nominations, including self-nominations, until 11:59 p.m. Eastern on Tuesday, January 19; nominees must be under 35 as of October 1, 2027 (born on or after October 2, 1992).
insights.speaker: Amy Nordrum
insights.so_what: Calendar marker: the resulting list is a recurring source of early-career founder and researcher names worth tracking.

insights.claim: Innovators Under 35 selection runs in stages: editors pick semifinalists who complete a formal application, then dozens of expert judges help choose the 35 honorees among scientists, entrepreneurs and inventors who show real-world impact.
insights.speaker: Amy Nordrum
insights.so_what: The multi-stage, judge-vetted process makes the list a reasonably filtered deal-sourcing input for early-stage tech.
insights.locator: After the deadline, our editors will review

insights.claim: MIT Technology Review has produced its Innovators Under 35 list since 1999 to help its reporters scout young talent and to introduce readers to rising stars, with emphasis on problems like human disease and climate change.
insights.speaker: Amy Nordrum
insights.so_what: Past lists and archives can be mined for founders whose companies later raise or exit—useful for venture sourcing in biotech and climate tech.
insights.quote: rising stars worth watching in the years to come
insights.locator: Our newsroom began producing our Innovators
